name: גֵּרְשׁוֹן
summary: The first named of Levi’s three sons (with Kohath and Merari), the father of Libni and Shimei; his sons, the Gershonites (גֵּרְשֻׁנִּי), camped west of the Dwelling and carried its curtains, coverings and hangings, and with the sons of Merari set out carrying the Dwelling (Num 10:17); they received thirteen cities with their open land. The name is the letters of גָּרַשׁ “drive out” with the ending ‑וֹן, so “driving out”, but scripture gives no reason for it. Chronicles also spells him גֵּרְשֹׁם, the name of Moses’ son, which Exodus explains by גֵּר “sojourner”, so the name may also have been heard that way.

evidence.note: “The sons of Levi: גֵּרְשׁוֹן, Kohath and Merari.”
Levi’s sons; the sons of Gershon, Libni and Shimei.
The Gershonite clans camp behind the Dwelling westward and keep its curtains, tent, covering and hangings.
The service of the Gershonites, to serve and to carry, under Ithamar.
“The Dwelling was taken down, and the sons of Gershon and the sons of Merari set out, carrying the Dwelling.”
Thirteen cities by lot from Issachar, Asher, Naphtali and half Manasseh.
Spelled גֵּרְשֹׁם: “The sons of Levi: Gershom, Kohath and Merari.”
Moses’ son גֵּרְשֹׁם: “for he said, I have been a sojourner (גֵּר) in a foreign land”; the explanation given for the other spelling.
The root’s verb: “cast out (גָּרֵשׁ) this bondwoman and her son.”
The root’s verb of Israel, “thrust out (גֹרְשׁוּ) of Egypt”.

note: bdb includes the gentilic גֵּרְשֻׁנִּי (c.di.af), which TIPNR files as a form of the person Gershon@Gen.46.11; drop it if gentilics should not be claimed by name entries. c.di.ad (גֵּרְשֹׁם) is not claimed: it is mainly Moses’ son (Gershom@Exo.2.22) and Gershom@Ezr.8.2, but also holds the Chronicles spelling of this Gershon, and shares six tokens with c.di.ae. The meaning “driving out” is the plain sense of the letters; no verse explains Gershon’s name, and the Exodus explanation belongs to Moses’ son.
